The narrowing of the confidence interval around the point estimate for shorter horizons, and its widening for longer horizons, is a natural reflection of increasing uncertainty as time progresses. While the provided intervals capture the expected range of outcomes under normal conditions, certain specific risks or "black swan" events could push the actual value outside these boundaries. These types of events are inherently difficult to model and predict, representing significant deviations from expected patterns that would invalidate the assumptions underlying the current forecast.
